WEST JAVA PROVINCE

WEST JAVA PROVINCE

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KARAWANG REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF KARAWANG,

Considering : a. that women as one of the community groups whose existence is a potential and development asset need to be empowered so that they can actualize their potential optimally to participate in development;

b. that women as a national asset who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to obtain guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination;

c. that in order to make effective a comprehensive and integrative system in empowering and protecting women in Karawang Regency, regulations regarding the empowerment and protection of women are needed;

d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Empowerment and Protection of Women;

In View of : 1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia;

2. Law Number 14 of 1950 concerning the Establishment of Regency Regions within West Java Province (State Gazette of the Republic of

Indonesia Number 9) as amended by

Law Number 4 of 1968 concerning

the Establishment of Purwakarta Regency and Subang Regency

by amending Law Number 14

of 1950 concerning the Establishment of Regency

Regions within West Java Province

(State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1968

Number 31, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of

Indonesia Number 2851);

3. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention On

The Elimination of All Form of Discrimination Againts

Women) (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of

1984 Number 29 Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of

Indonesia Number 3277);

4. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence

(State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004

Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of

Indonesia Number 4419);

5. Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to

the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587) as amended several times most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning

the Second Amendment to Law Number 23

of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State

Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number

With Mutual Approval of

THE REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF KARAWANG REGENCY and

THE REGENT OF KARAWANG

HAS DECIDED:

To Enact : REGIONAL REGULATION ON EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN.

Article 9

(1) Women who are victims of acts of violence have the right to receive protection, information, integrated services and continued handling.

(2) Continued handling as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out up to the rehabilitation stage.

(3) Continued handling as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out by individuals, groups, regional government institutions, and/or non-governmental institutions.

Article 15

(1) The Regional Government shall conduct monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and Protection of Women.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women in the Region.

(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies, programs and activities that implement policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and Protection of Women. (4) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be carried out from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Empowerment and Protection of Women for the current year.

Article 16

(1) The Regional Government shall conduct an evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Empowerment and Protection of Women at the end of each fiscal year in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) The evaluation results as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the following year.

Article 14

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups and/or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may take the form of:

a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 12

(1) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women in the Region as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (2) shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements.

(2) Membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, community, universities and/or community organizations.

(3) Provisions regarding the establishment and membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 18

Upon the entry into force of this Regional Regulation, all Regional laws and regulations related to the Empowerment and protection of women shall remain in effect insofar as they are not contrary to the provisions of this Regional Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Karawang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Karawang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration who lead the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
7. Women Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties, either temporarily or based on court decisions.
8. Task force is a semi-permanent working group, consisting of related regional apparatus work units, the community, universities, and/or community organizations chaired by the Regional Secretary, who are given additional tasks within a certain period of time, to implement certain programs/activities in the field of empowerment and protection of women.
9. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, community and state), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men into the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF WOMEN

Article 8

(1) Women empowerment is implemented to improve the position, role and quality of Women in family, community, and national life.

(2) Women Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed so that Women:

a. Obtain their opportunities and rights as human beings;
b. Are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities; and
c. Have equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 10

The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of Women Empowerment and Protection institutions in the Region.

Article 17

Funding for the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women shall be sourced from:

a. Regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VIII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

CHAPTER VII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 6

The rights of women in marriage and family are to: a. Choose her husband freely;

b. Marriage is based on the consent of both parties; and

c. Have the same rights and responsibilities both as parents to their children and as spouses.

CHAPTER III

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 20

This Regional Regulation shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placement in the Regional Gazette of Karawang Regency.

Stipulated in Karawang on 12 April 2017

Article 3

The Rights of Women in Employment include:

a. Having equal employment opportunities as men; b. Equal opportunities from the selection process, work facilities, benefits to the right to receive equal wages; c. Obtaining paid leave including maternity leave; and
d. Women cannot be dismissed by employers on the grounds of pregnancy or marital status.

Article 7

The rights of women in public and political life are the right to vote and be elected and to obtain equal opportunities to participate in the formulation of government policies up to their implementation.

CHAPTER IV

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 4

The rights of women in the field of Health include:

a. Freedom from death during childbirth; b. Obtaining health services, especially family planning services, pregnancy, childbirth and post-delivery.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Karawang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Karawang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration who lead the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
7. Women Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties, either temporarily or based on court decisions.
8. Article 18

Upon the entry into force of this Regional Regulation, all Regional laws and regulations related to the Empowerment and protection of women shall remain in effect insofar as they are not contrary to the provisions of this Regional Regulation.

Article 8

(1) Women empowerment is implemented to improve the position, role and quality of Women in family, community, and national life.

(2) Women Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed so that Women:

a. Obtain their opportunities and rights as human beings;
b. Are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities; and
c. Have equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 4

The rights of women in the field of Health include:

a. Freedom from death during childbirth; b. Obtaining health services, especially family planning services, pregnancy, childbirth and post-delivery.

Article 17

Funding for the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women shall be sourced from:

a. Regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 5

The right of women in the field of education is to obtain the opportunity to pursue education and receive scholarships.

3.9.text:
Article 9

(1) Women who are victims of acts of violence have the right to receive protection, information, integrated services and continued handling.

(2) Continued handling as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out up to the rehabilitation stage.

(3) Continued handling as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out by individuals, groups, regional government institutions, and/or non-governmental institutions.

CHAPTER VII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Karawang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Karawang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration who lead the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
7. Women Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties, either temporarily or based on court decisions.
8. Task force is a semi-permanent working group, consisting of related regional apparatus work units, the community, universities, and/or community organizations chaired by the Regional Secretary, who are given additional tasks within a certain period of time, to implement certain programs/activities in the field of empowerment and protection of women.
9. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, community and state), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men into the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.

Article 15

(1) The Regional Government shall conduct monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and Protection of Women.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women in the Region.

(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies, programs and activities that implement policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and Protection of Women. (4) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be carried out from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Empowerment and Protection of Women for the current year.

Article 14

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups and/or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may take the form of:

a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

This Regional Regulation shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placement in the Regional Gazette of Karawang Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Karawang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Karawang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration who lead the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
7. Women Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties, either temporarily or based on court decisions.
8. Task force is a semi-permanent working group, consisting of related regional apparatus work units, the community, universities, and/or community organizations chaired by the Regional Secretary, who are given additional tasks within a certain period of time, to implement certain programs/activities in the field of empowerment and protection of women.
9. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, community and state), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men into the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.

Article 15

(1) The Regional Government shall conduct monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and Protection of Women.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women in the Region.

(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies, programs and activities that implement policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and Protection of Women. (4) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be carried out from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Empowerment and Protection of Women for the current year.

Article 16

(1) The Regional Government shall conduct an evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Empowerment and Protection of Women at the end of each fiscal year in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) The evaluation results as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the following year.

Article 3

The Rights of Women in Employment include:

a. Having equal employment opportunities as men; b. Equal opportunities from the selection process, work facilities, benefits to the right to receive equal wages; c. Obtaining paid leave including maternity leave; and
d. Women cannot be dismissed by employers on the grounds of pregnancy or marital status.

Article 12

(1) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women in the Region as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (2) shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements.

(2) Membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, community, universities and/or community organizations.

(3) Provisions regarding the establishment and membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 18

Upon the entry into force of this Regional Regulation, all Regional laws and regulations related to the Empowerment and protection of women shall remain in effect insofar as they are not contrary to the provisions of this Regional Regulation.

Article 14

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups and/or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may take the form of:

a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 10

The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of Women Empowerment and Protection institutions in the Region.

CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF WOMEN

Article 17

Funding for the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women shall be sourced from:

a. Regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 4

The rights of women in the field of Health include:

a. Freedom from death during childbirth; b. Obtaining health services, especially family planning services, pregnancy, childbirth and post-delivery.

Article 8

(1) Women empowerment is implemented to improve the position, role and quality of Women in family, community, and national life.

(2) Women Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed so that Women:

a. Obtain their opportunities and rights as human beings;
b. Are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities; and
c. Have equality in enjoying the results of development.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 6

The rights of women in marriage and family are to: a. Choose her husband freely;

b. Marriage is based on the consent of both parties; and

c. Have the same rights and responsibilities both as parents to their children and as spouses.

Article 7

The rights of women in public and political life are the right to vote and be elected and to obtain equal opportunities to participate in the formulation of government policies up to their implementation.

CHAPTER VII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

CHAPTER VIII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 19

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation must be stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

Article 5

The right of women in the field of education is to obtain the opportunity to pursue education and receive scholarships.

Article 20

This Regional Regulation shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placement in the Regional Gazette of Karawang Regency.

(1) Women empowerment is implemented to improve the position, role and quality of Women in family, community, and national life.

(2) Women Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed so that Women:

a. Obtain their opportunities and rights as human beings;
b. Are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities; and
c. Have equality in enjoying the results of development.

CHAPTER VI

FUNDING

Article 15

(1) The Regional Government shall conduct monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and Protection of Women.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women in the Region.

(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies, programs and activities that implement policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and Protection of Women. (4) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be carried out from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Empowerment and Protection of Women for the current year.

Article 16

(1) The Regional Government shall conduct an evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Empowerment and Protection of Women at the end of each fiscal year in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) The evaluation results as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the following year.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 12

(1) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women in the Region as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (2) shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements.

(2) Membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, community, universities and/or community organizations.

(3) Provisions regarding the establishment and membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutional arrangements as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Karawang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Karawang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration who lead the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
7. Women Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties, either temporarily or based on court decisions.
8. Task force is a semi-permanent working group, consisting of related regional apparatus work units, the community, universities, and/or community organizations chaired by the Regional Secretary, who are given additional tasks within a certain period of time, to implement certain programs/activities in the field of empowerment and protection of women.
9. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, community and state), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men into the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.

Article 9

(1) Women who are victims of acts of violence have the right to receive protection, information, integrated services and continued handling.

(2) Continued handling as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out up to the rehabilitation stage.

(3) Continued handling as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out by individuals, groups, regional government institutions, and/or non-governmental institutions.

Article 14

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups and/or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may take the form of:

a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.
